title: Schema Design Best Practices
description: Architect maintainable, scalable, and performant Prisma schemas with proper indexing, audit trails, soft deletes, and naming standards.

data.text: Designing an elegant database schema requires balancing immediate development velocity with long-term query performance and operational stability. Following proven industry patterns prevents database rewrites as your data volume grows from thousands to millions of records.

data.title: Core Principles
items: **1. Always index foreign keys**: Prisma does not automatically create database indexes on relation scalar fields. If you query `post.findMany({ where: { authorId } })`, you must add `@@index([authorId])`.
**2. Consistent Primary Keys**: Standardize on either UUIDs (`@default(uuid())`) or CUIDs (`@default(cuid())`) across distributed tables to avoid ID collision and sequential enumeration attacks.
**3. Standardize Audit Timestamps**: Include `createdAt DateTime @default(now())` and `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` on all mutable business entities.
**4. Explicit Table & Column Mappings**: Use `@@map` and `@map` to decouple TypeScript camelCase properties from PostgreSQL snake_case table names.
**5. Design for Soft Deletes**: Add `deletedAt DateTime?` to critical models to preserve historical records and financial trails.

data.title: schema.prisma Golden Template
data.content: A comprehensive model showcasing foreign key indexing, soft deletion, and audit tracking.
data.code:
model Organization {
  id          String       @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name        String       @db.VarChar(120)
  slug        String       @unique @db.VarChar(60)
  createdAt   DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz
  updatedAt   DateTime     @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz
  deletedAt   DateTime?    @map("deleted_at") @db.Timestamptz

  memberships Membership[]

  @@index([deletedAt])
  @@map("organizations")
}

model Membership {
  id             String       @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  organizationId String       @map("organization_id") @db.Uuid
  userId         String       @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  role           Role         @default(MEMBER)
  createdAt      DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz

  organization   Organization @relation(fields: [organizationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user           User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([organizationId, userId], name: "org_user_unique")
  // CRITICAL: Explicitly index foreign key fields!
  @@index([organizationId])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("memberships")
}

data.title: Automate Formatting with `prisma format`
data.text: Always run `npx prisma format` before committing. It automatically aligns fields, cleans up whitespaces, and normalizes relation declarations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Foreign keys require explicit `@@index` declarations in Prisma to prevent slow sequential table scans.
Use `createdAt` and `updatedAt` on all operational entities.
Adopt UUID or CUID identifiers for modern cloud-native systems.
Format schemas with `npx prisma format` to maintain team consistency.
